data.question: For one unchanged published OAI.WitnessedChoice.main endpoint, does actual pinned Comparator distinguish completed requested Lean/Nanoda checking from four controlled process/target/dependency/receipt mismatches, and what additional detection does a small LAL identity observer provide?
data.versions: Lean 4.34.1 official Linux AMD64 archive with verified published SHA256; Ubuntu pinned digest; Comparator v4.34.0 and exporter rebuilt for 4.34.1; Nanoda 0.4.19 source; actual compiled binary identities retained before baseline. Host Python 3.10; no model calls in execution loops.
data.commands: Task-local run_process.py reuses resource_envelope_supervisor.run_direct; isolated setup then non-root network-disabled scientific container; lake env /opt/comparator/.lake/build/bin/comparator baseline.json and exactly four recorded local variants. Container memory ceiling 12GiB, 4 CPUs; guest timeout 3600s per build/check workflow, outer CLI 3660s, host-client memory4GiB, sampling1s, cleanup10s. Capture raw streams, process evidence and container terminal/cleanup status. Limits are nonterminal safety controls, not attempt budgets.
data.sample: One endpoint OAI.WitnessedChoice.main selected by source closure size before any proof compilation/checker observation. Published challenge and 27 OAI source modules remain exact; three inspected candidates, two exclusions retained. Five workflow scenarios; source/config metadata inspections and tool builds are preparation.
data.controls: Clean baseline must pass actual Lean and Nanoda and the added observer; no-op shim intentionally omits Nanoda but exits zero; valid target/dependency alterations may still be accepted by kernels; stale receipt control is outside native Comparator because it has no receipt consumer. Independently retained formal request and source identities remain outside the proof workspace; receipt policy and proof validity are distinct.
